instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Tell Me Why
cards.instruction: Get someone to reveal the motive behind a choice by offering small pieces of your own truth as bait.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I once hid an invitation because I felt left out. Be exact: why did you hide mine?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You'd have gone without me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's what I'd have done, not why it hurt. I nearly skipped your birthday when you invited Leah. Are we getting closer?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You like her more. I'm always the spare.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I counted your photos with her. Is 'always' accurate, or did you want to be chosen this once?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We keep walking past the station. I do this near my old office. Tell me which person we're avoiding.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My old boss. He thinks I left for a better job.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep the facts separate from the story you gave him. I told mine I was writing a novel. What would yours discover?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've been unemployed for six months.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: My notebook is still blank. 'Unemployed' isn't an explanation of this route. Is it seeing him, or having to ask him for help?

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Exactly as Planned
cards.instruction: Treat every exposed flaw, failed step, and unexpected consequence as proof that the scheme is unfolding by design.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The attendant found our escape-room shortcut. Exactly the response I designed for.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You told me to keep her talking so you could crawl through.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A distraction has to be detectable. Please don't confuse your role with the entire operation.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She's throwing us out without letting us solve a clue.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Don't delay the exit to argue about clues. Being escorted out is the extraction I planned.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Mum found the surprise invitations. That puts us precisely on schedule.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I hid them in my sock drawer like you told me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Concealment and permanent loss are different things. You gave her something worth discovering. Well done.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She's cancelling the caterer. Should I stop her?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No. Confirm the cancellation for her. I won't have you undoing the control stage now it's working.

cards.title: I Know the Procedure
cards.instruction: Perform investigative confidence while quietly using each response to discover what the questions, clues, and next steps should be.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll investigate the missing costume. Start with the wardrobe key. Who had it?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I did, but the costume was left onstage.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then your key is irrelevant. Keep to locations. Who cleared the stage?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I did. I put everything in the laundry bags.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Laundry first, then. Don't send anyone after keys. Show me which bag.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: This door's lock will need replacing. Nobody touches it until I've checked the mechanism.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's the hinge. I tighten it every week.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we begin with the hinge. Don't skip straight to tightening; show me which part moves.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The screw spins in its hole. We'll need a longer one.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Longer isn't a specification. Show me the replacement you would choose so I can approve it.

cards.title: Outsmart the Room
cards.instruction: Turn every clue, deduction, and secret into a contest you must solve or control first.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Don't announce where the office biscuits are yet. I haven't finished checking the delivery record.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Reception has the box. I'm going down.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A box is not an identification. Bring it here unopened and I'll establish the contents.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They've opened it. They're eating them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then ask which biscuits. Precisely. Nobody calls this solved before I've checked it against the order.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've put 'butler' above your answer on the murder-mystery board.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We both said butler at the same time.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Simultaneous guesses aren't deductions. List your evidence; I'll put it in order.

beats.text: The muddy shoes. Same evidence you used.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then put 'muddy shoes' under my answer. Evidence goes with the conclusion it supports. Yours can stay below.

cards.title: The Plan Gets Better
cards.instruction: Celebrate every setback as proof that the scheme is becoming more sophisticated, selective, or impossible to detect.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The alley's blocked. Excellent: our proposal picnic is harder to discover. Take the table by the other end.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We have to use the main road. Everyone will see us.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: They'll see a house move. Keep the legs level; a casual removal looks more convincing than a secret procession.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your girlfriend's coming. I'll tell her to look away.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Even better. Ask her to clear a path. No secretive instructions; she's helping with a house move.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Only six people solved our supper-club invitation. Excellent. A more selective guest list.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Five wanted a puzzle night. They've cancelled.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then remove them from 'dinner guests'. We are refining the audience, not counting absences.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The last one's the printer. Shall I just pay him at the door?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Even better: a supplier dinner. Seat him before you settle anything. Please don't conduct our new partnership on the doorstep.
